contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 15. Canonical Job fields

All canonical IDs use closed-loop-id/1. Agents and humans never choose canonical IDs. For each family, FIELD_REGISTRY supplies an exact uppercase ASCII family prefix. The application reserves an allocationSequence and collisionCounter in the same transaction and computes:

ID_PAYLOAD is the first 20 digest bytes in SHA-256 output order. base32hex uses alphabet `0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv`, most-significant-bit first, lowercase, with no padding. CANONICAL_ID = <FAMILY_PREFIX> + "-" + base32hex(ID_PAYLOAD).

The application begins collisionCounter at 0 and increments it only when the generated ID already exists for a different allocation tuple. The collision check and any increment occur inside the same transaction. Exact command retry returns the original ID from the idempotency receipt and does not reserve a new sequence. Content equality alone never collapses separately authorized records. Clone remapping uses the clone JOB_ID namespace and records the complete source-to-clone mapping. Every allocation receipt records the algorithm version, namespace, canonical input tuple, sequence, collision counter, collision check, resulting ID, command identity, and project revision.

entries.controllingText: promptIdentity.bodySha256 is the SHA-256 of the exact authoritative prompt-file bytes defined in Section 10.1.

atomicObligation.statement: promptIdentity.bodySha256 is the SHA-256 of the exact authoritative prompt-file bytes defined in Section 10.1.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: For every external-agent operation, the authoritative prompt is an application-generated file artifact. Its body is exactly the UTF-8 byte sequence of the exported prompt file, and promptIdentity.bodySha256 equals the application-computed SHA-256 of those exact bytes.

The current prompt-file contract is UTF-8 without BOM, LF line endings, no implicit line-ending conversion, no wrapper or header bytes outside the generated body, and a final newline required. Its media type is text/plain;charset=utf-8. Its canonical package path is `instruction.txt`. Its exported transport filename is <JOB_ID>_<STAGE_TWO_DIGITS>_<OPERATION>_<INSTRUCTION_ID>.txt after closed-loop-filename/1 normalization. The application preview is decoded from those authoritative bytes. Clipboard copy is optional and nonauthoritative and cannot create a second prompt identity.

The prompt file does not contain its own bodySha256 or any value whose computation depends on bodySha256. manifest.json carries promptIdentity, including the application-computed bodySha256, and the prompt instructs the external actor to echo the exact manifest promptIdentity. This avoids a self-referential prompt hash.
17.2 Prompt identity

All canonical IDs use closed-loop-id/1. Agents and humans never choose canonical IDs. For each family, FIELD_REGISTRY supplies an exact uppercase ASCII family prefix. The application reserves an allocationSequence and collisionCounter in the same transaction and computes:

ID_PAYLOAD is the first 20 digest bytes in SHA-256 output order. base32hex uses alphabet `0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv`, most-significant-bit first, lowercase, with no padding. CANONICAL_ID = <FAMILY_PREFIX> + "-" + base32hex(ID_PAYLOAD).

entries.controllingText: When staging or raw capture fails, canonical state does not change. The application preserves the staged bytes and slot identities when technically possible, identifies exactly what was and was not recorded, and permits retry without opening or pasting the file. When the browser requires reselection, the UI identifies the exact prior filename, size, and digest and classifies reselection as an unavoidable file action rather than repeated semantic resupply. The application never claims an uncaptured response was recorded.

An unverified external time claim remains SOURCE_ASSERTED. Where neither basis exists, the obligation remains UNKNOWN.

entries.controllingText: HUMAN_ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED is the default mode and is mandatory for Stage 01 COMPLETE and RECONCILE_INTAKE, wherever the proposal co-accepts a humanAuthorityCandidates confirmation under Section 14.10, and wherever the accepted result supersedes previously accepted current canonical records under a REPLACE_CURRENT_STAGE_SET policy. VALIDATED_AUTO_COMMIT is permitted only where the operation writes exclusively agent-owned fields into its own reserved target slot, carries no humanAuthorityCandidates, and embeds no genuine human-authority decision. Application commands never use proposal acceptance; they commit directly under Sections 22.4 and 36.12. The declared mode is closed and version-bound and cannot be altered by a response.

atomicObligation.statement: VALIDATED_AUTO_COMMIT is permitted only when an operation writes exclusively agent-owned fields into its own reserved target slot, carries no humanAuthorityCandidates, and embeds no genuine human-authority decision.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: A human-origin fact or decision first supplied inside an external-agent conversation does not become HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION authority merely because the agent reports it. The response places each such value in humanAuthorityCandidates with its external-response pointer and claimed conversation basis. The application presents the exact extracted value for direct confirm or correct without requiring retyping. Information already present in current raw input or accepted human records is not reconfirmed.

Exact confirmation may be co-accepted atomically with the dependent agent proposal: the transaction creates the new human input or decision record first, revalidates that the response declared and used the identical confirmed value, binds the proposal to the confirmation receipt, and commits both or neither. This special co-acceptance does not permit any unconfirmed human value. A correction, omitted candidate, inconsistent value, or any other scope-changing input invalidates the response and requires a replacement prompt. This rule applies at every stage.
17.12 Proposal-acceptance modes
Application-native deterministic results are application-owned.
They bypass external response ingestion.
They use a dedicated validated application command.
They do not require human proposal review.

Creation of an application-derived receipt, release calculation, evidence-chain calculation, registry calculation, or terminal determination MUST NOT invalidate itself merely because its own atomic commit increments the project revision. Each derived record binds to its precondition dependency closure and committed revision. Only a later mutation affecting that dependency closure makes it stale.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: A human-origin fact or decision first supplied inside an external-agent conversation does not become HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION authority merely because the agent reports it. Information already present in current raw input or accepted human records is not reconfirmed.

Exact confirmation may be co-accepted atomically with the dependent agent proposal: the transaction creates the new human input or decision record first, revalidates that the response declared and used the identical confirmed value, binds the proposal to the confirmation receipt, and commits both or neither. This special co-acceptance does not permit any unconfirmed human value. A correction, omitted candidate, inconsistent value, or any other scope-changing input invalidates the response and requires a replacement prompt. This rule applies at every stage.

All canonical semantic hashes use closed-loop-canonical-json/1. Its implementation contract fixes:

For every registered hash kind, the preimage inclusion set is exactly the canonical fields of the subject record or manifest, excluding only the digest field itself and every field whose value depends on that digest, fields declared audit-only or derived-summary, and fields the owning schema explicitly excludes with a registered reason. The scope-hash preimage is exactly the Section 14.7 dimensions of the operation, and the terminal-hash preimage is exactly the records enumerated in Section 36.9. An unregistered hash kind or pointer set is UNDEFINED_HASH_PREIMAGE and blocks the computation and every dependent gate. Default array semantics are ordered and order-significant; an array is set-valued only when its JSON pointer is explicitly registered with an element-identity key, a duplicate rule that rejects duplicates, and a sort rule of canonical byte order over the element identity. An unregistered pointer treated as a set is UNDEFINED_SET_SEMANTICS and blocks.

The deterministic profile governs application-produced archives only. An inbound archive from an external actor is a nonauthoritative convenience container: it must pass the Section 19.9 safety rules, is exploded into named attachment slots with per-member byte verification, and its original bytes are preserved as evidence. External actors are never required to produce the deterministic profile; the authoritative inbound representation remains response.json plus attachment-slot files.

Every artifact preserves rawFilename and has a safe displayFilename and canonicalPath under closed-loop-filename/1. Canonical comparison uses Unicode 15.1.0 NFC, case-sensitive identity, and separately checked Unicode 15.1.0 default-case-fold and registered platform-risk collision keys. Absolute paths, drive prefixes, NUL, control characters, empty segments, `.` and `..`, duplicate canonical paths, case-fold collisions, extraction-target collisions, and supported confusable collisions are rejected. An unauthorized rename never matches solely because bytes are equal.

File extension and browser MIME type are claims. Format-dependent work records the authorized parser or adapter and detected interpretation. A materially ambiguous polyglot is BLOCKED unless one interpretation is explicitly authorized and every alternate interpretation is harmless under the operation.

Archive intake and export fail closed on traversal, absolute paths, duplicate or colliding paths, symlinks, hard links, device entries, unsupported special files, unsupported or encrypted members outside a registered encrypted contract, unsupported compression, excessive nesting, entry count, per-entry size, total compressed or expanded size, compression ratio, path depth, filename length, Unicode ambiguity, manifest mismatch, unmanifested extra members, missing members, or modified bytes. Expansion occurs only in an isolated bounded parser path and never makes content executable or prompt-visible by itself.

Every artifact preserves rawFilename and has a safe displayFilename and canonicalPath under closed-loop-filename/1. An unauthorized rename never matches solely because bytes are equal.

entries.controllingText: Every registered operation declares named input ports, output ports, exact types, cardinalities, deterministic error codes, error propagation, and resource-cost category. Each operation declares exact input arity and types and one normalized output type. Multi-artifact branches use explicit step references. BYTE_COMPARE and COMPARE receive explicit left and right inputs. Assertions receive explicit actual and expected inputs. A failed or unknown predecessor prevents dependent execution and propagates the registered terminal disposition without partial canonical result; errors propagate as typed execution failure and no later step may consume a failed output. Intermediate step outputs exist only for the current execution unless explicitly emitted as observations or evidence.

entries.controllingText: The current registries are closed-loop-json-selector/1 and closed-loop-xml-selector/1. closed-loop-json-selector/1 MUST support at least: the root `$`; child access by identifier name and by single-quoted bracket name; nonnegative array index; and the wildcard `*` over object values and array elements. Selection order is document order. Recursive descent, filters, unions, slices, and script expressions are excluded from version 1. closed-loop-xml-selector/1 MUST support at least: absolute child-element paths from the document root; the element wildcard `*`; 1-based positional index predicates; attribute access `@name`; and `text()` value extraction. All other axes, predicates, and functions are excluded from version 1. A proposition that cannot be faithfully expressed within these registered subsets is not natively representable and routes externally.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: Every expected returned file has an application-owned ATTACHMENT_SLOT_ID bound to package, reservation, job, stage, operation, purpose, role, requiredness, allowed media type, filename rule, maximum size, and expected digest when known. The response attachment declaration references the slot ID and supplies claimed filename, media type, byte size, digest, and semantic role.

The operator selects each returned file into its named slot. Selection order and filename alone never establish mapping. A file may fill only the slots explicitly permitted by the contract. Duplicate use, missing required slots, ambiguous patterns, cross-package slots, unexpected extras, or actual-byte mismatch is rejected before proposal creation.
24.2 Returned attachment slots

Mapping by array order or filename alone is prohibited. Duplicate or ambiguous matches fail closed.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: The current canonical handoff container is a logical manifest plus separately selected exact files. Its identity is the SHA-256 of the canonical manifest, which lists every member by package-relative canonical path, ATTACHMENT_SLOT_ID or outbound role, byte length, hash algorithm, digest, media type, disclosure classification, and requiredness. Member order, file-picker order, download order, and archive order are nonauthoritative.
The canonical manifest contains packageManifestSha256 computed from closed-loop-canonical-json/1 with packageManifestSha256 omitted. No package digest includes itself.

An optional archive is only a transport representation of the same logical container. It must use the registered deterministic archive profile and pass the archive safety rules. The current profile is closed-loop-archive-profile/1: a ZIP archive containing only STORE (uncompressed) entries, entries ordered by canonical-path unsigned byte order, the UTF-8 filename flag set, every timestamp fixed to 1980-01-01T00:00:00, no directory entries, no symlinks or special entries, no archive comment, no encryption, and no extra fields except a Zip64 field exactly where an entry or archive size requires it. The manifest is always at `manifest.json`; the authoritative prompt is at `instruction.txt`; an inbound response is at `response.json`. Directory entries, timestamps, permissions, compression method, compression level, and path normalization are fixed by the registered archive profile. An archive mismatch does not alter the logical package identity; it rejects the transport representation.

The deterministic profile governs application-produced archives only. An inbound archive from an external actor is a nonauthoritative convenience container: it must pass the Section 19.9 safety rules, is exploded into named attachment slots with per-member byte verification, and its original bytes are preserved as evidence. External actors are never required to produce the deterministic profile; the authoritative inbound representation remains response.json plus attachment-slot files.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 25.2 Reservation and package transaction order
An external operation is established in one atomic transaction that:
1. verifies the current precondition revision and target slot;
2. checks the idempotency key before treating an exact retry as stale;

3. allocates commandId, OPERATION_RESERVATION_ID, challengeNonce, prompt identity, package identity, and target slot; challengeNonce contains at least 128 bits produced by `crypto.getRandomValues`, and the operation blocks if that CSPRNG is unavailable;
4. creates the exact prompt-file and package-manifest identities;
5. commits one reservationRevision;
6. returns the authoritative package bound to that committed reservationRevision.

If the transaction begins at project revision R, it commits reservationRevision = R + 1. The package expectedRevision and the response scope projectRevision are exactly reservationRevision. Acceptance requires the current project revision to equal reservationRevision except for an exact idempotent retry already covered by the receipt.

Reservation states are RESERVED, EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, RESPONSE_STAGED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED, CANCELLED, SUPERSEDED, or EXPIRED_BY_SCOPE. Only RESERVED, EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, and RESPONSE_STAGED can preserve package validity, and only when revision, scope, prompt, package, nonce, and target slot remain unchanged. EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, RESPONSE_STAGED, REJECTED, and CANCELLED are recorded as metadata-store operational events and do not increment canonical projectRevision. ACCEPTED commits the canonical project once. A later canonical scope change marks the reservation SUPERSEDED or EXPIRED_BY_SCOPE. No operational status event invalidates its own package.

Only RESERVED, EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, and RESPONSE_STAGED can preserve package validity, and only when revision, scope, prompt, package, nonce, and target slot remain unchanged. EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, RESPONSE_STAGED, REJECTED, and CANCELLED are recorded as metadata-store operational events and do not increment canonical projectRevision. ACCEPTED commits the canonical project once. A later canonical scope change marks the reservation SUPERSEDED or EXPIRED_BY_SCOPE. No operational status event invalidates its own package.

Resuming an ORPHANED reservation verifies the same binding and changes no identity. A new authoritative reservation for the slot is prohibited until the old reservation is terminal. An exact idempotent retry returns the original receipt even when the project has advanced to the command's committed revision. A different normalized payload under the same key is rejected.

entries.controllingText: The reservation state machine is the closed set defined in Section 35.6: RESERVED → EXPORTED → RESPONSE_STAGED → ACCEPTED, with ORPHANED, RESUMED, REJECTED, CANCELLED, SUPERSEDED, and EXPIRED_BY_SCOPE as the only recovery or terminal states, as defined by the operation registry. Resume of an ORPHANED reservation preserves its original binding when still current.

entries.controllingText: When author and reviewer disagree materially, neither output is promoted. A distinct reconciliation operation is required, and a distinct reconciler receives both completed outputs and the governing evidence. The reconciler differs from both contexts unless a genuine human-authority decision is required. A third reviewer is required when the reconciliation contract designates the dispute as technical semantic judgment and neither prior view can be rejected from objective evidence. A human may decide only an actual human authority, policy, scope, risk, disclosure, or tradeoff question. Every unresolved disagreement remains UNKNOWN or BLOCKED and is never automatically promoted.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 29.10 Activation-proposition proof

Every normative requirement has one primary PROPOSITION_ID. Independent truth conditions are split or represented by one accepted acyclic proof expression. Semantic sameness is established only by an independent EQUIVALENT review; wording, embeddings, filenames, and hashes cannot merge propositions.

The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

Every current applicable release-bearing proposition has exactly one current PROOF_OBLIGATION_ID identifying its proof expression, required leaves, evidence classes, allowed epistemic bases, artifacts, dependencies, freshness, independence, verification timing, current satisfaction, blockers, and scope hash. Optional, advisory, stale, historical, or unregistered results cannot satisfy it.

EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

Every release-bearing evidence path is EVIDENCE_RECORD → OBSERVATION_RECORD → proposition or proof leaf. An observation identifies exact subject, location or measurement point, finding, method/tool, inputs and outputs, hashes, origin, submitting actor, epistemic basis, time/freshness fields, source evidence, scope, and raw-response or native-execution provenance.

Every observation has an accepted relation ESTABLISHES, REFUTES, SUPPORTS_ONLY, CONTEXT_ONLY, DOES_NOT_ADDRESS, or UNKNOWN. Only ESTABLISHES provides affirmative proof; REFUTES provides failure evidence; SUPPORTS_ONLY and CONTEXT_ONLY cannot independently satisfy a proof obligation. Normalization never elevates an external claim.

Time-sensitive evidence records observedAt, its DEVICE_REPORTED, SOURCE_ASSERTED, or VERIFIED_EXTERNAL basis, validFrom, validUntil, supersession, freshness requirement, status, and reason. Required freshness that cannot be established is UNKNOWN. Current justificatory evidence is acyclic.

VERIFIED_EXTERNAL is achieved only under a registered attestation-verification contract fixing the evidence type, the attesting tool or system identity, the verification method, the bound inputs including the operation challengeNonce or reservation, the freshness rule, and the failure semantics. Absent such a registered contract, the basis remains EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED or weaker.

A future obligation is not treated as satisfied, violated, or missing before its target exists. It remains scheduled and cannot be omitted from the future closed obligation universe.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: The application derives DUE_NOW only when the current stage is at least EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE, the target-availability condition is TRUE, the obligation is current and applicable, and the current stage is at or beyond its REQUIRED_BY_STAGE. UNKNOWN target availability blocks only when the obligation could be due.

Stages 12, 13, 18, and 19 evaluate only current applicable PREPRODUCT_ITERATION obligations whose PER_RUN_REQUIRED value is TRUE and that are due by the relevant stage. Final-product, representation, delivery, evidence-closure, registry-closure, and terminal-delivery obligations do not block Stage 18 or Stage 19 before their targets exist, and Stages 12, 13, 18, and 19 MUST NOT require product-only, representation-only, delivery-only, or terminal-only propositions before their targets exist. They remain preserved as future required obligations and become due at their declared stages.

A deferred target-dependent test becomes due no earlier than the first stage where its target exists and no later than REQUIRED_BY_STAGE. It is never required before the target exists and is never represented as executed before actual execution.

entries.controllingText: TRUE requires affirmative support meeting the proof obligation. FALSE requires sufficient current evidence establishing noncompliance or negation. UNKNOWN applies when neither is established and fails closed wherever affirmative proof is required. Missing data is UNKNOWN unless a closed-universe rule affirmatively establishes FALSE. Contradictory sufficient evidence blocks and is never averaged away.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 29.13 Proposition and proof-expression contract

entries.controllingText: The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

entries.controllingText: EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

entries.controllingText: A controlled exception never converts a violated proposition into SATISFIED. It is either an authorized scope change creating new input and requirements versions, an authoritative waiver represented as a new governing obligation with its own proposition and evidence, or a blocker where authority is insufficient. Every exception records authority, reason, scope, effective period, affected propositions, independent challenge when obligations are reduced, and downstream invalidation.

entries.controllingText: Materiality is MATERIAL, NONMATERIAL, or UNKNOWN. MATERIAL means the item could change the truth value, applicability, proof admissibility, evidence sufficiency, identity, due state, dependency closure, gate result, authorization, or delivery status of at least one current release-bearing proposition or action. NONMATERIAL requires affirmative reasoning that the item cannot alter any current proposition, proof obligation, artifact identity, dependency, gate, release eligibility, delivery scope, or delivery state. UNKNOWN is treated as MATERIAL for exclusion and blocking. Every materiality determination that excludes content, reduces required work, or downgrades an obligation is recorded as a materialityReviews record; where it reduces a possible obligation it requires independent review under Section 26.5.

The author and reviewer cannot share the same raw response, context reservation, operation reservation, or accepted review identity. A reviewer cannot approve a semantic value it authored. Search adequacy, Stage 03 extraction challenge, Stage 04 disposition and atomicity, Stage 05 classification/applicability/equivalence, Stage 06 proof-expression, evidence-basis, and native-versus-external representability review, and Stage 26 semantic reconciliation use this contract.

When author and reviewer disagree materially, neither output is promoted. A distinct reconciliation operation is required, and a distinct reconciler receives both completed outputs and the governing evidence. The reconciler differs from both contexts unless a genuine human-authority decision is required. A third reviewer is required when the reconciliation contract designates the dispute as technical semantic judgment and neither prior view can be rejected from objective evidence. A human may decide only an actual human authority, policy, scope, risk, disclosure, or tradeoff question. Every unresolved disagreement remains UNKNOWN or BLOCKED and is never automatically promoted.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 30.7 Release disposition
The application applies this distinction.

A contradiction that contains sufficient refutation of an applicable mandatory proposition does not prevent REJECTED under Section 36.4 rule 1; contradiction produces BLOCKED only where no sufficient mandatory refutation already controls.
1. If current sufficient evidence REFUTES any current applicable mandatory proposition, SELECTED_RELEASE_STATE = REJECTED.

2. Otherwise, if any required proposition, applicability, proof obligation, evidence relation, freshness state, independence condition, dependency, due test, artifact, challenge, contradiction, or capability is UNKNOWN, stale, incomplete, insufficient, or blocked, SELECTED_RELEASE_STATE = BLOCKED.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: The application derives DUE_NOW only when the current stage is at least EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE, the target-availability condition is TRUE, the obligation is current and applicable, and the current stage is at or beyond its REQUIRED_BY_STAGE. UNKNOWN target availability blocks only when the obligation could be due.

Stages 12, 13, 18, and 19 evaluate only current applicable PREPRODUCT_ITERATION obligations whose PER_RUN_REQUIRED value is TRUE and that are due by the relevant stage. Final-product, representation, delivery, evidence-closure, registry-closure, and terminal-delivery obligations do not block Stage 18 or Stage 19 before their targets exist, and Stages 12, 13, 18, and 19 MUST NOT require product-only, representation-only, delivery-only, or terminal-only propositions before their targets exist. They remain preserved as future required obligations and become due at their declared stages.
31. Ten-run stability and reliability metrics

A run execution attempt that ends REJECTED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED never counts toward the exactly-ten requirement and cannot satisfy any matrix cell. Its reservation reaches a terminal state, the same run target slot is re-reserved under Section 35.6, and the replacement attempt receives a new fresh context reserved for that run. The superseded context becomes historical, is excluded from the ten-distinct-context calculation, and its outputs cannot appear in any authorized input. Exactly the ten current accepted runs and their ten current distinct contexts satisfy Stage 11. An accepted run is never re-executed within the same iteration; a defect discovered in an accepted run routes through Stages 13-17.

Completion: The complete current required relation set exists for every due PER_RUN_REQUIRED proposition, run, and test. Every verifier satisfies the semantic-review independence contract. Every required tuple has sufficient evidence and exactly one valid determination; no nondue or meaningless Cartesian cell is manufactured.

Completion: Every due PER_RUN_REQUIRED mandatory proposition has one comparison covering all ten current runs under its frozen expected-variance contract. Allowed variance is recorded; prohibited variance has a defect; UNKNOWN variance remains blocked.

UNKNOWN target availability blocks only when the obligation could be due.

Stages 12, 13, 18, and 19 evaluate only current applicable PREPRODUCT_ITERATION obligations whose PER_RUN_REQUIRED value is TRUE and that are due by the relevant stage. Final-product, representation, delivery, evidence-closure, registry-closure, and terminal-delivery obligations do not block Stage 18 or Stage 19 before their targets exist, and Stages 12, 13, 18, and 19 MUST NOT require product-only, representation-only, delivery-only, or terminal-only propositions before their targets exist. They remain preserved as future required obligations and become due at their declared stages.
31. Ten-run stability and reliability metrics
Project-level operational metrics include:

A run execution attempt that ends REJECTED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED never counts toward the exactly-ten requirement and cannot satisfy any matrix cell. Its reservation reaches a terminal state, the same run target slot is re-reserved under Section 35.6, and the replacement attempt receives a new fresh context reserved for that run. The superseded context becomes historical, is excluded from the ten-distinct-context calculation, and its outputs cannot appear in any authorized input. Exactly the ten current accepted runs and their ten current distinct contexts satisfy Stage 11. An accepted run is never re-executed within the same iteration; a defect discovered in an accepted run routes through Stages 13-17.

Completion: The complete current required relation set exists for every due PER_RUN_REQUIRED proposition, run, and test. Every verifier satisfies the semantic-review independence contract. Every required tuple has sufficient evidence and exactly one valid determination; no nondue or meaningless Cartesian cell is manufactured.

Completion: Every due PER_RUN_REQUIRED mandatory proposition has one comparison covering all ten current runs under its frozen expected-variance contract. Allowed variance is recorded; prohibited variance has a defect; UNKNOWN variance remains blocked.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: Every external, human, tool, system, physical, publication, filing, purchase, security, or production action is classified before package generation as one or more of:

The action contract records exact target, scope, expected effect, reversibility, maximum cost where applicable, legal or authority dependency where applicable, containment, rollback or stop condition, responsible actor, and required authorization. READ_ONLY or demonstrably safe REVERSIBLE actions may proceed under the normal stage authority. Any other class requires a current purpose- and target-bound HUMAN_DECISION before execution. UNKNOWN blocks. A test or prompt may never authorize action beyond the recorded target and risk scope.

Negative, adversarial, destructive, or security tests use isolated disposable state or an explicitly authorized bounded external sandbox. Canonical user projects and third-party systems are not mutation targets merely because a test requires an invalid state.

Canonical user projects and third-party systems are never mutation targets unless the exact action is separately authorized and safely bounded.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: Every external, human, tool, system, physical, publication, filing, purchase, security, or production action is classified before package generation as one or more of:

The action contract records exact target, scope, expected effect, reversibility, maximum cost where applicable, legal or authority dependency where applicable, containment, rollback or stop condition, responsible actor, and required authorization. READ_ONLY or demonstrably safe REVERSIBLE actions may proceed under the normal stage authority. Any other class requires a current purpose- and target-bound HUMAN_DECISION before execution. UNKNOWN blocks. A test or prompt may never authorize action beyond the recorded target and risk scope.

Negative, adversarial, destructive, or security tests use isolated disposable state or an explicitly authorized bounded external sandbox. Canonical user projects and third-party systems are not mutation targets merely because a test requires an invalid state.

Confusable detection uses the Unicode Technical Standard #39 confusables data published for Unicode 15.1.0. These exact data identities and table digests are recorded in the runtime registry and deployment manifest. A host Unicode implementation may be used only when startup and CI conformance fixtures establish the pinned results for every supported code-point class; otherwise the application uses bundled pinned tables. An unknown host/table mismatch blocks canonical filename normalization and package activation. Runtime upgrades do not silently change canonical identities; runtime or browser Unicode behavior may not silently redefine canonical identity. Every contentSha256, recordSha256, project hash, package hash, proof hash, scope hash, and terminal hash has a closed JSON-pointer inclusion and omission set registered in workflow-schema.js. entries.controllingText: For every registered hash kind, the preimage inclusion set is exactly the canonical fields of the subject record or manifest, excluding only the digest field itself and every field whose value depends on that digest, fields declared audit-only or derived-summary, and fields the owning schema explicitly excludes with a registered reason. The scope-hash preimage is exactly the Section 14.7 dimensions of the operation, and the terminal-hash preimage is exactly the records enumerated in Section 36.9. An unregistered hash kind or pointer set is UNDEFINED_HASH_PREIMAGE and blocks the computation and every dependent gate. Default array semantics are ordered and order-significant; an array is set-valued only when its JSON pointer is explicitly registered with an element-identity key, a duplicate rule that rejects duplicates, and a sort rule of canonical byte order over the element identity. An unregistered pointer treated as a set is UNDEFINED_SET_SEMANTICS and blocks.

Each matrix entry is statically classified as INPUT_CURRENT, TARGET_RESERVED, or IMMUTABLE_REFERENCE by STAGE_OPERATION_SCOPE_MATRIX. Creation operations use application-reserved target identities for the version or record they create; they do not pretend that the target already exists. A dimension designated by this matrix is required and non-null. A scope dimension not designated for the operation is prohibited unless the registry marks it as an immutable referenced target. An unregistered hash kind or pointer set is UNDEFINED_HASH_PREIMAGE and blocks the computation and every dependent gate. Default array semantics are ordered and order-significant; an array is set-valued only when its JSON pointer is explicitly registered with an element-identity key, a duplicate rule that rejects duplicates, and a sort rule of canonical byte order over the element identity. An unregistered pointer treated as a set is UNDEFINED_SET_SEMANTICS and blocks.

Each matrix entry is statically classified as INPUT_CURRENT, TARGET_RESERVED, or IMMUTABLE_REFERENCE by STAGE_OPERATION_SCOPE_MATRIX. Creation operations use application-reserved target identities for the version or record they create; they do not pretend that the target already exists. Read dependencies use current input identities. The response echoes both classes in their registered locations, and the application verifies every input current and every target still reserved.

A dimension designated by this matrix is required and non-null. A scope dimension not designated for the operation is prohibited unless the registry marks it as an immutable referenced target. Missing, extra, stale, unreserved, or inconsistent dimensions are rejected before proposal creation or command execution.

entries.controllingText: The application begins collisionCounter at 0 and increments it only when the generated ID already exists for a different allocation tuple. The collision check and any increment occur inside the same transaction. Exact command retry returns the original ID from the idempotency receipt and does not reserve a new sequence. Content equality alone never collapses separately authorized records. Clone remapping uses the clone JOB_ID namespace and records the complete source-to-clone mapping. Every allocation receipt records the algorithm version, namespace, canonical input tuple, sequence, collision counter, collision check, resulting ID, command identity, and project revision.

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: No other stage-operation combination is valid. The registry declares for each listed operation its allowed response types, target-slot derivation, required input families, writable fields and collections, reservation requirement, independence requirement, completion predicate, retry behavior, and whether it is agent, human, or application executed.

- External-agent operations are COMPLETE at Stages 01-09, 15, 21, 23, 24, 25, and 26; SEMANTIC_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_INTAKE; SEARCH_ADEQUACY_REVIEW; RECONCILE_SOURCE_SEARCH; RECONCILE_RESEARCH; DISPOSITION_CHALLENGE; ATOMICITY_CHALLENGE; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENTS; SEMANTIC_REVIEW; RECONCILE_REQUIREMENT_SET; PROOF_REVIEW; RECONCILE_VERIFICATION_SUITE; EXECUTE_RUN; VERIFY; COMPARE; ROOT_CAUSE; REGRESSION; CORRECT; RECONCILE at Stage 26; ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27; EXECUTE_EXTERNAL_TEST; INVESTIGATE_MISSING_EVIDENCE; and EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST, EXECUTE_REGRESSION, and REGRESSION_VERIFY when externally routed. They require an operation reservation and file-first package. Their responseType is exactly DATA_PROPOSAL, HUMAN_INPUT_REQUIRED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED as permitted by the operation's field contract. ADVISORY_REVIEW at Stage 27 is optional and non-gating: it writes releaseGateReviews records only and cannot modify, delay, or substitute for any CALCULATE_RELEASE input, calculation, or state.

- Application commands are EXECUTE_FAILURE_TEST when natively routed, EXECUTE_REGRESSION when natively routed, REGRESSION_VERIFY when natively routed, FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, COMPLETE at Stage 18, CONFIRM at Stage 19, FREEZE_BASELINE, RUN_NATIVE_TESTS, RUN_NATIVE_ATTACKS, FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE, VERIFY_IDENTITY, CALCULATE_RELEASE, CALCULATE_EVIDENCE_CHAINS, and CALCULATE_TERMINAL. They accept no external response envelope and commit only application-owned results through the universal command path. COMPLETE at Stage 18 and CONFIRM at Stage 19 are application-calculated convergence and confirmation determinations; agents contribute only the separately declared explanatory fields of the owning record families. FREEZE, CONFIRM_FREEZE, FREEZE_BASELINE, and FREEZE_DELIVERY_CANDIDATE consume and reference the required current humanDecisions records; they never create human authority.

- HUMAN_DECISION commands are CAPTURE_DELIVERY_INTENT; application confirmation of a newly reported human-origin answer; and RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION, one global application-validated command bound to exactly one registered purpose and target per invocation. The closed RECORD_HUMAN_DECISION purpose enum is INTENT_CONFIRMATION, CANDIDATE_COMPONENT_SELECTION, BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, DISCLOSURE_AUTHORIZATION, EXTERNAL_ACTION_RISK_AUTHORIZATION, CONTROLLED_EXCEPTION, REGRESSION_RETIREMENT_AUTHORIZATION, BACKUP_POLICY_SELECTION, TRADEOFF_OR_SCOPE_DECISION, VISUAL_BASELINE_AUTHORIZATION, and HUMAN_AUTHORITY_CORRECTION. Each purpose writes only the humanDecisions record and the human-decision-owned fields FIELD_REGISTRY declares for that purpose and target. HUMAN commands are SAVE_HUMAN_INPUT, which creates and edits User Job Input and saves Section 18 fallback answers with their declared consequences, and RECORD_HUMAN_OBSERVATION, which records human-owned observation and evidence records for human-inspection routes. These commands write only their declared HUMAN or HUMAN_DECISION fields and records, accept no agent-owned canonical fields, and accept no external response envelope.

- EXPORT_PROMPT_FILE, EXPORT_EXECUTION_PACKAGE, SELECT_RESPONSE_JSON_FILE, SELECT_RETURNED_FILES, EXPORT_OR_SHARE_AUTHORIZED_ARTIFACTS, and RECORD_DELIVERY_EVIDENCE are operator actions. They create only the application receipts and human or external evidence explicitly declared by their contracts.

For every operation, TARGET_SLOT = SHA-256(closed-loop-canonical-json/1 of contractProfileId, jobId, stage, operation, and all operation-specific target identities required by Section 14.7). The target slot excludes projectRevision so an exact retry retains its slot; expectedRevision and scopeHash remain separate mandatory preconditions. No operation can write a family or field not listed in its FIELD_REGISTRY entry.

- A CURRENT_* pointer or version field designated Nullable: Yes is null exactly until its owning stage first creates the referenced version or record, is non-null thereafter, and never reverts to null; a superseding creation moves it to the new current identity.
- A field with a Required stage is required and non-null at and after acceptance of that stage; before that stage it is absent under its declared registry contract rather than silently defaulted.
- LATEST_EVIDENCE_REFERENCE is null exactly until the first canonical evidence record exists.

- CURRENT_ITERATION and CURRENT_CANDIDATE_ID carry the closed-loop-id/1 identities of the iterations and candidateFreezes families; every other CURRENT_* identity or version field carries the application-allocated identity of its owning family or version registry.

- CURRENT_STATE is the closed enum BLOCKED, AWAITING_HUMAN_INPUT, PROPOSAL_PENDING_REVIEW, RESPONSE_STAGED, AWAITING_EXTERNAL_RESPONSE, READY_FOR_NEXT_OPERATION, and WORKFLOW_COMPLETE; exactly one value is derived, and when more than one condition holds the earliest value in this list controls.
- JOB_RECORD_STATUS is the closed enum INCOMPLETE, BLOCKED, and COMPLETE; a Stage 01 correction or invalidation returns it to INCOMPLETE.
- runId, sourceConvergedIterationId, and confirmationIterationId are anchored by their application-reserved operation targets and their owning canonical records rather than by job-level pointers.

The application derives DUE_NOW only when the current stage is at least EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE, the target-availability condition is TRUE, the obligation is current and applicable, and the current stage is at or beyond its REQUIRED_BY_STAGE. UNKNOWN target availability blocks only when the obligation could be due.

Stages 12, 13, 18, and 19 evaluate only current applicable PREPRODUCT_ITERATION obligations whose PER_RUN_REQUIRED value is TRUE and that are due by the relevant stage. Final-product, representation, delivery, evidence-closure, registry-closure, and terminal-delivery obligations do not block Stage 18 or Stage 19 before their targets exist, and Stages 12, 13, 18, and 19 MUST NOT require product-only, representation-only, delivery-only, or terminal-only propositions before their targets exist. They remain preserved as future required obligations and become due at their declared stages.

A deferred target-dependent test becomes due no earlier than the first stage where its target exists and no later than REQUIRED_BY_STAGE. It is never required before the target exists and is never represented as executed before actual execution.

Independence is recorded separately for APPLICATION_SESSION_DISTINCTNESS, APPLICATION_INPUT_ISOLATION, USER_TRANSFER_CONFORMITY, EXTERNAL_CONTEXT_IDENTIFIER_DISTINCTNESS, PROVIDER_CONTEXT_INDEPENDENCE, EXECUTOR_OR_REVIEWER_ROLE_SEPARATION, and ENVIRONMENT_INDEPENDENCE where required. APPLICATION_ESTABLISHED means only that application-observable dimensions required by the contract are satisfied. Distinct IDs do not prove hidden provider-state independence. A required UNKNOWN dimension blocks or leaves the result undetermined.

Every external operation contract declares MINIMUM_INPUT_BINDING_BASIS from APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, and SELF_ASSERTED. An echoed manifest identity and per-member digests establish at most EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED. SELF_ASSERTED or UNKNOWN cannot satisfy an operation whose contract requires byte-exact input possession, and gates derive admissibility from the recorded basis.

Every release-bearing proposition, applicability condition, independence condition, entailment conclusion, source-authenticity conclusion, environment claim, and external-capability claim carries truthValue TRUE, FALSE, or UNKNOWN; epistemicBasis APPLICATION_OBSERVED, VERIFIED_EXTERNAL, EXTERNALLY_SUPPORTED, SELF_ASSERTED, or NONE; currentScopeStatus CURRENT or STALE; freshnessStatus CURRENT, EXPIRED, UNKNOWN, or NOT_APPLICABLE; contradictionStatus CLEAR or CONTRADICTED; reasons; supportingEvidenceIds; and a derivation or accepted semantic-review identity.

TRUE requires affirmative support meeting the proof obligation. FALSE requires sufficient current evidence establishing noncompliance or negation. UNKNOWN applies when neither is established and fails closed wherever affirmative proof is required. Missing data is UNKNOWN unless a closed-universe rule affirmatively establishes FALSE. Contradictory sufficient evidence blocks and is never averaged away.

The closed proof-expression language permits LEAF, ALL_OF, ANY_OF, and AT_LEAST_K only. It has no arbitrary code, unrestricted negation, implicit coercion, stale references, or empty operators. ALL_OF is TRUE when all children are TRUE, FALSE when any is FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. ANY_OF is TRUE when any is TRUE, FALSE when all are FALSE, and UNKNOWN otherwise. AT_LEAST_K is TRUE when trueCount ≥ K, FALSE when trueCount + unknownCount < K, and UNKNOWN otherwise.

EQUIVALENT applies only to proposition-to-proposition sameness. The relation between a test and a proof leaf, and between a proof expression and its proposition, is sufficiency, established by the accepted Stage 06 PROOF_REVIEW. A LEAF references exactly one of: a canonical test with its required disposition, an observation-backed proposition, an applicability or activation condition, or a prerequisite proof obligation; each leaf declares its truth extraction, required evidence classes, and scope binding, and no other leaf target is valid in version 1. An ANY_OF expression is accepted only when the review establishes that each branch alone suffices to establish the parent proposition; an AT_LEAST_K expression is accepted only when every permitted K-combination suffices or an explicitly reviewed combinatorial sufficiency contract covers it. A branch that weakens proof strength is rejected at Stage 06.

A contradiction that contains sufficient refutation of an applicable mandatory proposition does not prevent REJECTED under Section 36.4 rule 1; contradiction produces BLOCKED only where no sufficient mandatory refutation already controls.

An empty denominator is SATISFIED only when a current independently reviewed evidence-supported EMPTY_UNIVERSE determination exists for that metric. Otherwise the metric is UNKNOWN or BLOCKED; it is never automatically 100%. A missing trigger record, missing reservation, missing test, or missing proposition cannot make coverage pass by removing itself from the denominator.

For every registered hash kind, the preimage inclusion set is exactly the canonical fields of the subject record or manifest, excluding only the digest field itself and every field whose value depends on that digest, fields declared audit-only or derived-summary, and fields the owning schema explicitly excludes with a registered reason. The scope-hash preimage is exactly the Section 14.7 dimensions of the operation, and the terminal-hash preimage is exactly the records enumerated in Section 36.9. An unregistered hash kind or pointer set is UNDEFINED_HASH_PREIMAGE and blocks the computation and every dependent gate. Default array semantics are ordered and order-significant; an array is set-valued only when its JSON pointer is explicitly registered with an element-identity key, a duplicate rule that rejects duplicates, and a sort rule of canonical byte order over the element identity. An unregistered pointer treated as a set is UNDEFINED_SET_SEMANTICS and blocks.

All canonical IDs use closed-loop-id/1. Agents and humans never choose canonical IDs. For each family, FIELD_REGISTRY supplies an exact uppercase ASCII family prefix. The application reserves an allocationSequence and collisionCounter in the same transaction and computes:

ID_PAYLOAD is the first 20 digest bytes in SHA-256 output order. base32hex uses alphabet `0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv`, most-significant-bit first, lowercase, with no padding. CANONICAL_ID = <FAMILY_PREFIX> + "-" + base32hex(ID_PAYLOAD).

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: 35.2 Integrity
A project with failed integrity validation is read-only and cannot be recalculated, normalized, migrated in place, used for prompts, or made current. The only actions are:
- view integrity diagnostics;
- export exact raw project and artifact bytes with a quarantine manifest;
- restore a verified backup into a separate validated activation path;
- clone from an independently auditable source when permitted;
- delete the quarantined project.
No action silently converts quarantined data into current canonical state.

entries.controllingText: Reservation states are RESERVED, EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, RESPONSE_STAGED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED, CANCELLED, SUPERSEDED, or EXPIRED_BY_SCOPE. Only RESERVED, EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, and RESPONSE_STAGED can preserve package validity, and only when revision, scope, prompt, package, nonce, and target slot remain unchanged. EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, RESPONSE_STAGED, REJECTED, and CANCELLED are recorded as metadata-store operational events and do not increment canonical projectRevision. ACCEPTED commits the canonical project once. A later canonical scope change marks the reservation SUPERSEDED or EXPIRED_BY_SCOPE. No operational status event invalidates its own package.

entries.controllingText: closed-loop-encrypted-export/1 uses AES-256-GCM with a fresh 96-bit cryptographically random IV per encrypted payload, a fresh 128-bit random salt, PBKDF2-HMAC-SHA-256 with 600,000 iterations to derive the 256-bit key from the operator passphrase, and the canonical unencrypted package manifest digest as authenticated additional data. The container records algorithm, KDF, iterations, salt, IV, ciphertext length, and authentication tag. The passphrase and derived key are never persisted. IV reuse under one key is prohibited. Authentication failure rejects the export or restore without partial activation. CREDENTIAL_SECRET backup material requires this encrypted profile and cannot use an acknowledgment-only unencrypted export.

Package creation uses a derived allowlist, prohibited-member exclusion, known secret-pattern scan, path scan, disclosure check, and supported metadata inventory. A clean heuristic scan is not proof of absence. Redaction creates a new artifact and never silently replaces the original.

entries.controllingText: A run execution attempt that ends REJECTED, BLOCKED, or EXECUTION_FAILED never counts toward the exactly-ten requirement and cannot satisfy any matrix cell. Exactly the ten current accepted runs and their ten current distinct contexts satisfy Stage 11. contextSourceLocations.controllingText: An external operation is established in one atomic transaction that:

If the transaction begins at project revision R, it commits reservationRevision = R + 1. The package expectedRevision and the response scope projectRevision are exactly reservationRevision. Acceptance requires the current project revision to equal reservationRevision except for an exact idempotent retry already covered by the receipt.

Reservation states are RESERVED, EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, RESPONSE_STAGED, ACCEPTED, REJECTED, CANCELLED, SUPERSEDED, or EXPIRED_BY_SCOPE. Only RESERVED, EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, and RESPONSE_STAGED can preserve package validity, and only when revision, scope, prompt, package, nonce, and target slot remain unchanged. EXPORTED, ORPHANED, RESUMED, RESPONSE_STAGED, REJECTED, and CANCELLED are recorded as metadata-store operational events and do not increment canonical projectRevision. ACCEPTED commits the canonical project once. A later canonical scope change marks the reservation SUPERSEDED or EXPIRED_BY_SCOPE. No operational status event invalidates its own package.

Resuming an ORPHANED reservation verifies the same binding and changes no identity. A new authoritative reservation for the slot is prohibited until the old reservation is terminal. An exact idempotent retry returns the original receipt even when the project has advanced to the command's committed revision. A different normalized payload under the same key is rejected.

entries.controllingText: Verification completeness is:

atomicObligation.statement: Verification completeness ranges over required REQ_ID × RUN_ID × TEST_ID relations, subject to current applicability, verification phase, PER_RUN_REQUIRED and due-stage rules; it is not an indiscriminate product of all IDs.

sourceSpans.text: Verification completeness is:

contextSourceLocations.controllingText: The application derives DUE_NOW only when the current stage is at least EARLIEST_EXECUTABLE_STAGE, the target-availability condition is TRUE, the obligation is current and applicable, and the current stage is at or beyond its REQUIRED_BY_STAGE. UNKNOWN target availability blocks only when the obligation could be due.

Stages 12, 13, 18, and 19 evaluate only current applicable PREPRODUCT_ITERATION obligations whose PER_RUN_REQUIRED value is TRUE and that are due by the relevant stage. Final-product, representation, delivery, evidence-closure, registry-closure, and terminal-delivery obligations do not block Stage 18 or Stage 19 before their targets exist, and Stages 12, 13, 18, and 19 MUST NOT require product-only, representation-only, delivery-only, or terminal-only propositions before their targets exist. They remain preserved as future required obligations and become due at their declared stages.
36.3 Exact verification matrix
REQ_ID × RUN_ID × TEST_ID
Each verifier receives only the target run or blind alias, target requirements, tests, required artifacts, and governing evidence.

Completion: The complete current required relation set exists for every due PER_RUN_REQUIRED proposition, run, and test. Every verifier satisfies the semantic-review independence contract. Every required tuple has sufficient evidence and exactly one valid determination; no nondue or meaningless Cartesian cell is manufactured.

entries.controllingText: RESPONSIBLE_STAGE_MAP is mechanically derived: every canonical family maps to its Section 38 declared stage, and every global family maps to the earliest stage whose gate consumes it; a mutation in a family invalidates from that stage under Section 36.1. Registry findings are classified TERMINAL_ONLY_DEFECT, which blocks Stage 30 only, or PREMISE_REFUTING_DEFECT, which invalidates from the mapped responsible stage. A defect in the release-calculation semantics themselves is an implementation defect handled through the Sections 40-44 regression discipline, never by silently recalculating Stage 27.

38. Canonical record families and target ownership
The following record families remain the target model.
sources
- ID: SOURCE_ID
- Stage: 2
- Policy: REPLACE_CURRENT_STAGE_SET
- Agent owns substantive source description and classification.
- Application owns identity, version, and local-copy hash.
sourceConflicts
- ID: CONFLICT_ID
- Stage: 2
- Policy: APPEND_SCOPED
- Relationships: source A, source B, blocker.
- Agent owns semantic conflict analysis.
- Application owns identity and typed relationships.
research
- ID: RESEARCH_ID
- Stage: 3
- Policy: REPLACE_CURRENT_STAGE_SET
- Relationship: SOURCE_ID
- Agent owns extracted findings.
- Application owns identity and source relationship.
candidateRequirements
- ID: CANDIDATE_REQ_ID
- Stage: 3
- Policy: REPLACE_CURRENT_STAGE_SET
- Relationship: SOURCE_ID
- Agent owns source location, candidate obligation, classification, applicability, dependencies, and evidence.
- Application owns identity, source relationship, and status.
requirements
- ID: REQ_ID
- Stage: 4
- Policy: REPLACE_CURRENT_STAGE_SET
- Relationship: SOURCE_ID where applicable.
- Agent owns requirement meaning.
- Application owns identity and status.
- Every Stage 04 obligation-manifest identity has a typed trace to a requirement or explicit non-requirement disposition.
requirementResolutions
- ID: RESOLUTION_ID
- Stage: 5
- Policy: REPLACE_CURRENT_STAGE_SET
- Agent owns defect and resolution substance.
- Application owns identity, resulting requirements version, and status.
tests
- ID: TEST_ID
- Stage: 6
- Policy: REPLACE_CURRENT_STAGE_SET
- Relationship: REQ_ID
- Agent owns human-readable test semantics and Test IR content.
- Application owns identity, status, Test IR version, normalized Test IR hash, and binding validation.
- Native route is valid only when every operation is registered.
failureTests
- ID: MUTATION_ID
- Stage: 7
- Policy: REPLACE_CURRENT_STAGE_SET
- Relationships: requirement and validator defect.
- Gate independently proves actual execution, route capability, actual rejection, evidence sufficiency, and defect linkage.
instructions
- ID: INSTRUCTION_ID
- Stage: 8
- Policy: REPLACE_CURRENT_STAGE_SET
- Agent owns substantive instruction.
- Application owns identity.
preflightRecords
- ID: REVIEW_ID
- Stage: 9
- Policy: REPLACE_CURRENT_STAGE_SET
- Relationship: instruction.
- Agent owns findings.
- Application owns identity and relationship.
iterations
- ID: ITERATION_ID
- Stage: 10
- Policy: APPLICATION_DERIVED
- Application owns all fields.
candidateFreezes
- ID: CANDIDATE_ID
- Stage: 10
- Policy: APPLICATION_DERIVED
- Application owns all identity, manifest, versions, hashes, configuration, and status fields.
- Human component selection is a HUMAN_DECISION referenced through humanDecisions and never synthesized.
runs
- ID: RUN_ID
- Stage: 11
- Policy: UPDATE_RESERVED
- Agent owns execution observations and complete output.
- Application owns run, iteration, candidate, context identities, and output hashes.
- Candidate equality, context uniqueness, package equality, and contamination consequences are application-derived.
verification
- ID: VERIFICATION_ID
- Stage: 12
- Policy: APPEND_SCOPED
- Relationships: requirement, run, test, defect.
- Agent owns observations and evidence claims.
- Application owns identities, independence consequence, evidence-sufficiency consequence, and normalized gate outcome.
comparisons
- ID: COMPARISON_ID
- Stage: 13
- Policy: APPEND_SCOPED
- Agent owns semantic comparison observations.
- Application owns identity and all aggregates and stability diagnostics.
defects
- ID: DEFECT_ID
- Stage: 14
- Policy: APPEND_ONLY
- Agent owns substantive defect observations.
- Application owns identity, typed relationships, and lifecycle state.
rootCauses
- ID: RCA_ID
- Stage: 14
- Policy: APPEND_SCOPED
- Agent owns semantic RCA.
- Application owns identity and defect relationship.
regressions
- ID: REG_ID
- Stage: 15
- Policy: APPEND_ONLY
- Agent owns fixture, reproduction, detection, correction, and applicability.
- Application owns identity, fixture hash, lifecycle, and summaries derived only from actual regression executions.
changes
- ID: CHANGESET_ID
- Stage: 16
- Policy: APPEND_SCOPED
- Agent owns substantive correction proposal and impact analysis.
- Application owns identity and authorization consequences.
convergenceRecords
- ID: CONVERGENCE_ID
- Stage: 18
- Policy: APPLICATION_DERIVED
- Application owns all metrics and convergence state.
- Agent may explain failed conditions.
confirmationRecords
- ID: CONFIRMATION_ID
- Stage: 19
- Policy: APPEND_SCOPED
- Application derives unchanged state, completeness, new-defect counts, new-requirement counts, variance, contradictions, and final determination.
baselines
- ID: BASELINE_ID
- Stage: 20
- Policy: APPLICATION_DERIVED
- Human authorization is a HUMAN_DECISION referenced through humanDecisions and never synthesized.
- Application owns identity, bytes, hashes, versions, lineage, and status.
products
- ID: PRODUCT_ID
- Stage: 21
- Policy: UPDATE_RESERVED
- Agent owns execution observations.
- Application owns product identity, version, baseline, execution identity, context, instruction version, artifact inventory, and status.
deterministicResults
- ID: RESULT_ID
- Stage: 22
- Policy: APPEND_SCOPED

- All gate-consumed canonical fields are application-owned, including executor classification, runtime or external capability identity, Test IR identity, expected result, normalized actual result, determination, evidence relationship, and status.
- External observations exist only as submitted evidence before normalization.
meaningResults
- ID: MEANING_REVIEW_ID
- Stage: 23
- Policy: APPEND_SCOPED
- Agent owns product location, required and observed meaning, evidence comparison, and proposed determination.
- Application owns identities, independence consequence, evidence-sufficiency consequence, and normalized determination.
adversarialResults
- ID: ATTACK_ID
- Stage: 24
- Policy: APPEND_SCOPED
- Agent owns attack observations.
- Application owns identities, normalized determination, counts, independence consequence, and defect relationships.
representationInspections
- ID: INSPECTION_ID
- Stage: 25
- Policy: APPEND_SCOPED
- Irreducible observations belong to the proper agent or human authority.
- Objective filename, version, byte size, hash, transformation identity, and defect relationship are application-derived.
processAudits
- ID: PROCESS_AUDIT_ID
- Stage: 26
- Policy: REPLACE_CURRENT_STAGE_SET
- Agent owns semantic review.
- Application owns identity, missing-link detection, scope reconciliation, and contradiction consequences.
productAudits
- ID: PRODUCT_AUDIT_ID
- Stage: 26
- Policy: REPLACE_CURRENT_STAGE_SET
- Agent owns semantic review.
- Application owns identity and all counts.
releaseGateReviews
- ID: GATE_REVIEW_ID

- Agent provides advisory review only.
- Agent cannot set release.
releaseRecords
- ID: RELEASE_ID
- Stage: 27
- Policy: APPLICATION_DERIVED
- Application owns every field and determination.
artifactIdentities
- ID: IDENTITY_ID
- Stage: 28
- Policy: APPLICATION_DERIVED

evidenceInvestigations
- ID: INVESTIGATION_ID
- Stage: 29
- Policy: APPEND_SCOPED

- Application owns identity and requirement relationship.
evidenceChains
- ID: CHAIN_ID
- Stage: 29
- Policy: APPLICATION_DERIVED

instructionTraces

- unknown operation property is rejected;
- missing operation argument is rejected;
- wrong argument type is rejected;
- invalid artifact binding is rejected;
- cross-project artifact binding is rejected;
- stale artifact binding is rejected;
- unsupported selector syntax is rejected;
- invalid UTF-8 produces the correct disposition;
- explicit CSV configuration is honored;
- XML selector uses only the registered subset;
- regex pattern-size limit is enforced;
- regex input-size limit is enforced;
- IR step limit is enforced;
- input-byte limit is enforced;
- parsed-depth limit is enforced;
- worker timeout terminates execution;
- timeout creates no partial deterministic result;
- arbitrary JavaScript is impossible;
- arbitrary Python is impossible;
- shell execution is impossible;
- worker network access is unavailable;
- one-artifact binding works;
- multi-artifact binding works;
- BYTE_COMPARE detects equality and inequality;
- HASH_SHA256 matches application hash authority;
- integer exactness is preserved;
- approximate numeric comparison requires explicit tolerance;
- precision-sensitive floating equality is not silently used;
- normalized Test IR hash is stable;
- semantic Test IR change changes its hash;
- native execution records exact input hashes and runtime version;
- native result uses a dedicated application command;
- native result requires no human proposal review;
- external response cannot fabricate a native receipt;
- unsupported native operation blocks or routes externally;
- Stage 22 automatically runs all current ready native tests;
- one failed native mandatory test rejects the product;
- execution failure remains distinct from violation;
- product change invalidates native results;
- test-spec change invalidates native results;
- only current sufficient native results enter release and evidence-chain calculations.
The Test IR suite also covers:
- explicit stepId uniqueness;
- topological ordering;
- cycle rejection;
- forward-reference rejection;
- explicit named input and output ports;
- missing and extra port rejection;
- left/right operand identity for COMPARE and BYTE_COMPARE;
- multi-artifact branching;
- nonadjacent prior-step references;
- deterministic predecessor-error propagation;
- operation-registry digest verification;
- parser, selector, and regex registry identity;
- stale-result invalidation after a semantic registry change;
- no semantic change under a compatibility-only registry migration.
43. Test the tests
For every new gate class, the suite must:
1. create a deliberately invalid state;
2. prove the test detects it;
3. repair the state;
4. prove progression.
Required mutations include:
- duplicate context;
- generator/verifier context reuse;
- stripped artifact bytes;
- prose substituted for objective evidence;
- conflicting result;
- stale iteration;
- wrong candidate;
- prior-run sentinel leaked into prompt context;
- missing return attachment;
- modified artifact hash;
- unsupported Test IR operation;
- worker timeout;
- external attempt to set an application-owned result;
- incomplete Stage 01 raw-input accounting;
- incomplete Stage 01 semantic mapping;
- uninspected Stage 01 file;
- incomplete Stage 04 obligation accounting;
- repeated Stage 04 request for already captured user intent;
- unauthorized visual change;
- prompt-box size regression.
An assertion that never fails against an intentional invalid fixture is not accepted as meaningful coverage.

Every intentional invalid state is created in a disposable project, test-only database namespace, immutable artifact copy, worker-isolated byte set, or explicitly authorized external sandbox. The suite must verify both defect detection and absence of mutation to any canonical user project or unauthorized external target.
44. Negative test matrix
The acceptance suite covers, at minimum:
- malformed JSON;
- truncated JSON;
- Markdown-wrapped JSON;
- duplicate-member JSON;
- oversized JSON;
- wrong prompt identity;
- wrong contract identity;
- wrong context identity;
- wrong revision;
- wrong stage;
- wrong operation;
- wrong scope;
- ownership attacks;
- invalid types;
- invalid enums;
- prohibited nulls;
- non-finite numbers;
- invalid required empties;
- unresolved relationships;
- duplicate relationships;
- wrong cardinality;
- cross-project relationships;
- stale relationships;
- missing provenance;
- wrong evidence relationship;
- missing bytes;
- mismatched bytes;
- duplicate proposal;
- stale proposal;
- storage failure at every durable transaction boundary;
- fabricated Stage 02 authority;
- invalid no-source determination;
- incomplete Stage 03 source coverage;
- incomplete Stage 04 obligation coverage;
- non-atomic requirements;
- incomplete Stage 06 coverage;
- unavailable mandatory capability;
- unexecuted failure fixture;
- incomplete instruction trace;
- non-independent preflight;
- candidate mismatch;
- fewer than ten runs;
- more than ten runs;
- context reuse;
- incomplete verification matrix;
- omitted run in comparison;
- missing RCA;
- regression without failure reproduction;
- correction without new version;
- incomplete repeated iteration;
- false convergence;
- changed unchanged-confirmation candidate;
- baseline without confirmation;
- product without exact baseline lineage;
- weak Stage 22 evidence;
- incomplete meaning review;
- incomplete adversarial review;
- incomplete representation inspection;
- inconsistent process/product audit;
- false release;
- order-dependent artifact identity;
- insufficient evidence chain;
- rewritten append-only history;
- corrupt import;
- wrong package identity;
- wrong embedded artifact hash;
- migration creating Stage 31;
- Test IR code-injection attempts;
- worker resource-limit failures;
- blind-alias remapping failure;
- Stage 01 prompt generated without required file handoff;
- Stage 01 output accepted despite uninspected file;
- Stage 01 accepted despite omitted raw unit;
- Stage 04 prompt generated from incomplete Stage 01 or Stage 03 state;
- later stage prompting the human to retype accepted information;
- app asking the user to select a stored file again;
- unrelated CSS changes;
- live application failure despite green source tests.
Every injected storage failure proves complete commit or no canonical state change.
The negative matrix additionally covers:
- required clipboard use;
- prompt-file BOM, line-ending, wrapper, and final-newline mutation;
- response imported from wrong file identity;
- unmapped, duplicate, cross-package, or order-mapped attachment slots;

- stage-data/canonical-record disagreement;

- missing activation proof;
- Stage 25/Stage 28 delivery-candidate mismatch;
- terminal self-invalidation and Stage 27/Stage 30 dependency cycle;
- immediately stale package caused by reservation creation;
- delete or clone duplicate effect;
- Test IR implicit dataflow, forward references, cycles, and wrong ports;
- registry semantic drift under an unchanged identity;
- canonicalization drift across pinned fixtures;
- ID namespace collision;
- handoff package member-order dependence;
- disabled challenge thresholds;
- artificially narrow source universe;
- vacuous 100% metric;
- unpinned or stale physical iPhone acceptance;
- in-origin backup represented as external recovery;

- delivery authorization reused outside recipient or channel scope;
- delivery claimed from authorization alone;
- unauthorized destructive, costly, third-party, security, physical, or irreversible external action;

- DOM, HTML, CSS, attribute, URL-scheme, origin, and filename injection;
- unexpected deployment origin, base path, redirect, or cross-origin resource;

- human approval required for an application-owned calculation.

- Stage 03 omission challenges;
- Stage 04 disposition and atomicity challenges;
- normative-classification reviews;
- applicability and activation reviews;
- proof obligations and evidence-requirement reviews;

- backup policies and backup checkpoints;
- materiality reviews;
- registered derivations and normalizers;
- delivery-candidate sets;
